question_en:
I am verifying the official mission records of multi-wavelength observation facilities shown in the figure. Please start from the space observatory positioned lowest in the gamma-ray band and read the full mission name, the `Launch` date, and the band or observation target listed on the page. If the `Launch` year is 2009, stop immediately; otherwise, continue in the direction of increasing wavelength: within each band, visit from bottom to top, and from left to right when at the same height; after visiting all, proceed to the next band on the right. Ground-based and airborne facilities are not included in this verification. Please answer the following questions:
1. Which space observatories were visited in order? List them as "Name in Figure—Full Mission Name—Launch—Band or Observation Target" exactly as they appear on the official pages.
2. How many different mission pages were verified in total?
3. Which mission was the final one?

Answer Format: Please answer in numbered points (1)–(3); for Question 1, use a table to list the four mission fields in order, preserving the original text from the pages; for Question 2, provide the total number of pages in text; for Question 3, provide the final mission in text.
answer:
(1)

| Visit Order | Name in Figure | Full Mission Name | Launch | Band or Observation Target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Fermi | Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope | June 11, 2008 | Gamma rays |
| 2 | Swift | Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory | Nov. 20, 2004 | Multiwavelength |
| 3 | NuSTAR | Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array | June 13, 2012 | Target: Universe |
| 4 | Chandra | Chandra X-ray Observatory | July 23, 1999 | Target: Universe |
| 5 | GALEX | Galaxy Evolution Explorer | April 28, 2003 | Target: Universe |
| 6 | Hubble | Hubble Space Telescope | APR 24, 1990 | Objective: Understand the Universe |
| 7 | Kepler | Kepler / K2 | March 6, 2009 | Objective: Search for exoplanets |

(2) A total of 7 different mission pages were verified.

(3) Kepler (Kepler / K2).
